1	# Dot-com vs AI Bubble Comparison Dataset
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	Four datasets capturing key market metrics across two technology-driven market booms: the 1997–2002 dot-com era and the 2021–2024 AI era. The data is structured for side-by-side temporal alignment using a common `quarter_offset` or `year` field within each era.
     5	
     6	## Data Source
     7	
     8	### nasdaq_index
     9	Quarterly NASDAQ Composite closing values, rebased to 100 at the start of each era. Fields: `era` (string: "Dot-com" or "AI"), `quarter_offset` (integer 0–23), `label` (calendar quarter string), `index_value` (float). The dot-com series spans 24 quarters (1997-Q1 to 2002-Q4); the AI series spans 16 quarters (2021-Q1 to 2024-Q4).
    10	
    11	### pe_ratio
    12	Trailing 12-month P/E ratio for the NASDAQ Composite, sampled at irregular quarterly intervals. Fields: `era`, `quarter_offset`, `label`, `pe` (float, ratio). Dot-com P/E ranges from ~28 to ~105; AI-era P/E ranges from ~24 to ~40.
    13	
    14	### ipo_counts
    15	Annual count of technology-sector IPOs on US exchanges. Fields: `era`, `year` (integer), `ipo_count` (integer). Dot-com era: 6 years; AI era: 4 years.
    16	
    17	### corporate_earnings
    18	Aggregate annual net income for NASDAQ-100 companies in nominal billion USD. Fields: `era`, `year`, `earnings_bn` (float; may be negative). Dot-com earnings range from −12.3 to 30.5 B; AI-era earnings range from 358 to 510 B.
    19	
    20	## Data Notes
    21	- NASDAQ index values are rebased independently per era; absolute levels differ dramatically.
    22	- P/E ratios for the dot-com era include periods of near-zero aggregate earnings, inflating the ratio.
    23	- Nominal earnings are not inflation-adjusted; direct magnitude comparison across eras should note the ~20-year gap.
    24	- 2024 figures are estimates based on analyst consensus as of late 2024.

1	# Mermaid.js Diagram Types
     2	
     3	Comprehensive syntax reference for all 24+ diagram types in Mermaid.js v11.
     4	
     5	## Core Diagrams
     6	
     7	### Flowchart
     8	Process flows, decision trees, workflows.
     9	
    10	**Syntax:**
    11	```
    12	flowchart {direction}
    13	  {nodeId}[{label}] {arrow} {nodeId}[{label}]
    14	```
    15	
    16	**Directions:** TB/TD (top-bottom), BT, LR (left-right), RL
    17	**Shapes:** `()` round, `[]` rect, `{}` diamond, `{{}}` hexagon, `(())` circle
    18	**Arrows:** `-->` solid, `-.->` dotted, `==>` thick
    19	**Subgraphs:** Group related nodes
    20	
    21	### Sequence Diagram
    22	Actor interactions, API flows, message sequences.
    23	
    24	**Syntax:**
    25	```
    26	sequenceDiagram
    27	  participant A as Actor
    28	  A->>B: Message
    29	  activate B
    30	  B-->>A: Response
    31	  deactivate B
    32	```
    33	
    34	**Arrows:** `->` solid, `->>` arrow, `-->` dotted, `-x` cross, `-)` async
    35	**Features:** Loops, alternatives, parallel, optional, critical regions
    36	
    37	### Class Diagram
    38	OOP structures, inheritance, relationships.
    39	
    40	**Syntax:**
    41	```
    42	classDiagram
    43	  class Animal {
    44	    +String name
    45	    -int age
    46	    +void eat()
    47	  }
    48	  Animal <|-- Dog : inherits
    49	```
    50	
    51	**Visibility:** `+` public, `-` private, `#` protected, `~` package
    52	**Relationships:** `<|--` inheritance, `*--` composition, `o--` aggregation, `-->` association
    53	
    54	### State Diagram
    55	State machines, transitions, workflows.
    56	
    57	**Syntax:**
    58	```
    59	stateDiagram-v2
    60	  [*] --> State1
    61	  State1 --> State2 : transition
    62	  State2 --> [*]
    63	```
    64	
    65	**Features:** Composite states, choice points, forks/joins, concurrency
    66	
    67	### ER Diagram
    68	Database relationships, schemas.
    69	
    70	**Syntax:**
    71	```
    72	erDiagram
    73	  CUSTOMER ||--o{ ORDER : places
    74	  ORDER ||--|{ LINE_ITEM : contains
    75	```
    76	
    77	**Cardinality:** `||` one, `|o` zero-one, `}|` one-many, `}o` zero-many
    78	
    79	## Planning Diagrams
    80	
    81	### Gantt Chart
    82	Project timelines, schedules.
    83	
    84	**Syntax:**
    85	```
    86	gantt
    87	  title Project
    88	  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
    89	  section Phase1
    90	    Task1 :done, 2024-01-01, 5d
    91	    Task2 :active, after Task1, 3d
    92	```
    93	
    94	**Status:** `done`, `active`, `crit`, `milestone`
    95	
    96	### User Journey

    98	
    99	**Syntax:**
   100	```
   101	journey

   103	  section Shopping
   104	    Browse: 5: Customer
   105	    Add to cart: 3: Customer, System
   106	```
   107	
   108	**Scores:** 1-5 satisfaction levels
   109	
   110	### Kanban
   111	Task boards, workflow stages.
   112	
   113	**Syntax:**
   114	```
   115	kanban
   116	  Todo[Task Board]
   117	    task1[Implement API]
   118	    @{ assigned: "Dev1", priority: "High" }

   123	### Quadrant Chart

   128	quadrantChart

   133	
   134	## Architecture Diagrams

   147	### Architecture Diagram

   160	### Block Diagram

1	# Mermaid.js CLI Usage
     2	
     3	Command-line interface for converting Mermaid diagrams to SVG/PNG/PDF.
     4	
     5	## Installation
     6	
     7	**Global Install:**
     8	```bash
     9	npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
    10	```
    11	
    12	**Local Install:**
    13	```bash
    14	npm install @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
    15	./node_modules/.bin/mmdc -h
    16	```
    17	
    18	**No Install (npx):**
    19	```bash
    20	npx -p @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli mmdc -h
    21	```
    22	
    23	**Docker:**
    24	```bash
    25	docker pull ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli
    26	```
    27	
    28	**Requirements:** Node.js ^18.19 || >=20.0
    29	
    30	## Basic Commands
    31	
    32	**Convert to SVG:**
    33	```bash
    34	mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.svg
    35	```
    36	
    37	**Convert to PNG:**
    38	```bash
    39	mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.png
    40	```
    41	
    42	**Convert to PDF:**
    43	```bash
    44	mmdc -i input.mmd -o output.pdf
    45	```
    46	
    47	Output format determined by file extension.
    48	
    49	## CLI Flags
    50	
    51	**Core Options:**
    52	- `-i, --input <file>` - Input file (use `-` for stdin)
    53	- `-o, --output <file>` - Output file path
    54	- `-t, --theme <name>` - Theme: default, dark, forest, neutral
    55	- `-b, --background <color>` - Background: transparent, white, #hex
    56	- `--cssFile <file>` - Custom CSS for styling
    57	- `--configFile <file>` - Mermaid configuration file
    58	- `-h, --help` - Show all options
    59	
    60	**Example with All Options:**
    61	```bash
    62	mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o output.png \
    63	  -t dark \
    64	  -b transparent \
    65	  --cssFile custom.css \
    66	  --configFile mermaid-config.json
    67	```
    68	
    69	## Advanced Usage
    70	
    71	**Stdin Piping:**
    72	```bash
    73	cat diagram.mmd | mmdc --input - -o output.svg
    74	
    75	# Or inline
    76	cat << EOF | mmdc --input - -o output.svg
    77	graph TD
    78	  A[Start] --> B[End]
    79	EOF
    80	```
    81	
    82	**Batch Processing:**
    83	```bash
    84	for file in *.mmd; do
    85	  mmdc -i "$file" -o "${file%.mmd}.svg"
    86	done
    87	```
    88	
    89	**Markdown Files:**
    90	Process markdown with embedded diagrams:
    91	```bash
    92	mmdc -i README.template.md -o README.md
    93	```
    94	
    95	## Docker Workflows
    96	
    97	**Basic Docker Usage:**
    98	```bash
    99	docker run --rm \
   100	  -u $(id -u):$(id -g) \
   101	  -v /path/to/diagrams:/data \
   102	  ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli \
   103	  -i diagram.mmd -o output.svg
   104	```
   105	
   106	**Mount Working Directory:**
   107	```bash
   108	docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data \
   109	  ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli \
   110	  -i /data/input.mmd -o /data/output.png
   111	```
   112	
   113	**Podman (with SELinux):**
   114	```bash
   115	podman run --userns keep-id --user ${UID} \
   116	  --rm -v /path/to/diagrams:/data:z \
   117	  ghcr.io/mermaid-js/mermaid-cli/mermaid-cli \
   118	  -i diagram.mmd
   119	```
   120	
   121	## Configuration Files
   122	
   123	**Mermaid Config (JSON):**
   124	```json
   125	{
   126	  "theme": "dark",
   127	  "look": "handDrawn",
   128	  "fontFamily": "Arial",
   129	  "flowchart": {
   130	    "curve": "basis"
   131	  }
   132	}
   133	```
   134	
   135	**Usage:**
   136	```bash
   137	mmdc -i input.mmd --configFile config.json -o output.svg
   138	```
   139	
   140	**Custom CSS:**
   141	```css
   142	.node rect {
   143	  fill: #f9f;
   144	  stroke: #333;
   145	}
   146	.edgeLabel {
   147	  background-color: white;
   148	}
   149	```
   150	
   151	**Usage:**
   152	```bash
   153	mmdc -i input.mmd --cssFile styles.css -o output.svg
   154	```
   155	
   156	## Node.js API
   157	
   158	**Programmatic Usage:**
   159	```javascript
   160	import { run } from '@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli';
   161	
   162	await run('input.mmd', 'output.svg', {
   163	  theme: 'dark',
   164	  backgroundColor: 'transparent'
   165	});
   166	```
   167	
   168	**With Options:**
   169	```javascript
   170	import { run } from '@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli';
   171	
   172	await run('diagram.mmd', 'output.png', {
   173	  theme: 'forest',
   174	  backgroundColor: '#ffffff',
   175	  cssFile: 'custom.css',
   176	  configFile: 'config.json'
   177	});
   178	```
   179	
   180	## Common Workflows
   181	
   182	**Documentation Generation:**
   183	```bash
   184	# Convert all diagrams in docs/
   185	find docs/ -name "*.mmd" -exec sh -c \
   186	  'mmdc -i "$1" -o "${1%.mmd}.svg"' _ {} \;
   187	```
   188	
   189	**Styled Output:**
   190	```bash
   191	# Create dark-themed transparent diagrams
   192	mmdc -i architecture.mmd -o arch.png \
   193	  -t dark \
   194	  -b transparent \
   195	  --cssFile animations.css
   196	```
   197	
   198	**CI/CD Pipeline:**
   199	```yaml
   200	# GitHub Actions example
   201	- name: Generate Diagrams
   202	  run: |
   203	    npm install -g @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli
   204	    mmdc -i docs/diagram.mmd -o docs/diagram.svg
   205	```
   206	
   207	**Accessibility-Enhanced:**
   208	```bash
   209	# Diagrams with accTitle/accDescr preserved
   210	mmdc -i accessible-diagram.mmd -o output.svg
   211	```
   212	
   213	## Troubleshooting
   214	
   215	**Permission Issues (Docker):**
   216	Use `-u $(id -u):$(id -g)` to match host user permissions.
   217	
   218	**Large Diagrams:**
   219	Increase Node.js memory:
   220	```bash
   221	NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=4096" mmdc -i large.mmd -o out.svg
   222	```
   223	
   224	**Validation:**
   225	Check syntax before rendering:
   226	```bash
   227	mmdc -i diagram.mmd -o /dev/null || echo "Invalid syntax"
   228	```

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.ticker import MaxNLocator

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Color scheme - editorial, professional
dotcom_color = '#C44E52'  # Warm terracotta/red
ai_color = '#4C72B0'       # Cool steel blue
peak_dotcom = '#8B0000'    # Dark red for peak marker
peak_ai = '#1A3A5C'        # Dark blue for peak marker
grey = '#555555'
light_grey = '#AAAAAA'
bg_color = '#FEFEFE'
grid_color = '#E8E8E8'

# Extract data
# NASDAQ index
nasdaq = data['nasdaq_index']['data']
ndx_dotcom = [(d['quarter_offset'], d['index_value']) for d in nasdaq if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ndx_ai = [(d['quarter_offset'], d['index_value']) for d in nasdaq if d['era'] == 'AI']
ndx_dotcom_x, ndx_dotcom_y = zip(*ndx_dotcom)
ndx_ai_x, ndx_ai_y = zip(*ndx_ai)

# P/E ratio
pe = data['pe_ratio']['data']
pe_dotcom = [(d['quarter_offset'], d['pe']) for d in pe if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
pe_ai = [(d['quarter_offset'], d['pe']) for d in pe if d['era'] == 'AI']
pe_dotcom_x, pe_dotcom_y = zip(*pe_dotcom)
pe_ai_x, pe_ai_y = zip(*pe_ai)

# IPO counts
ipos = data['ipo_counts']['data']
ipo_dotcom = [(d['year'], d['ipo_count']) for d in ipos if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
ipo_ai = [(d['year'], d['ipo_count']) for d in ipos if d['era'] == 'AI']

# Corporate earnings
earnings = data['corporate_earnings']['data']
earn_dotcom = [(d['year'], d['earnings_bn']) for d in earnings if d['era'] == 'Dot-com']
earn_ai = [(d['year'], d['earnings_bn']) for d in earnings if d['era'] == 'AI']

# Map year to quarter offset for annual data
def year_to_offset(year, base_year):
    return (year - base_year) * 4 + 1.5

ipo_dotcom_x = [year_to_offset(y, 1997) for y, _ in ipo_dotcom]
ipo_dotcom_y = [c for _, c in ipo_dotcom]
ipo_ai_x = [year_to_offset(y, 2021) for y, _ in ipo_ai]
ipo_ai_y = [c for _, c in ipo_ai]

earn_dotcom_x = [year_to_offset(y, 1997) for y, _ in earn_dotcom]
earn_dotcom_y = [e for _, e in earn_dotcom]
earn_ai_x = [year_to_offset(y, 2021) for y, _ in earn_ai]
earn_ai_y = [e for _, e in earn_ai]

# Peak markers
dotcom_peak_offset = 12  # 2000-Q1 (March 2000 peak = ~Q1 2000)
ai_peak_offset = 15       # 2024-Q4 (recent high)

# Create figure
fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 1, figsize=(14, 16), sharex=False, 
                         gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [1.2, 1, 1, 1], 'hspace': 0.08})
fig.patch.set_facecolor(bg_color)

# Global styling
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'DejaVu Sans'
plt.rcParams['font.size'] = 10
plt.rcParams['axes.labelcolor'] = grey
plt.rcParams['xtick.color'] = grey
plt.rcParams['ytick.color'] = grey

# ---- Panel 1: NASDAQ Index ----
ax1 = axes[0]
ax1.set_facecolor(bg_color)
ax1.plot(ndx_dotcom_x, ndx_dotcom_y, color=dotcom_color, linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=4, label='Dot-com (1997–2002)')
ax1.plot(ndx_ai_x, ndx_ai_y, color=ai_color, linewidth=2.5, marker='s', markersize=4, label='AI Era (2021–2024)')

# Peak markers
ax1.axvline(x=dotcom_peak_offset, color=peak_dotcom, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.7)
ax1.axvline(x=ai_peak_offset, color=peak_ai, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.7)

# Peak annotations
ax1.annotate('Dot-com Peak\n(Mar 2000)', xy=(dotcom_peak_offset, max(ndx_dotcom_y)), 
            xytext=(dotcom_peak_offset-1.5, max(ndx_dotcom_y)+20),
            fontsize=9, color=peak_dotcom, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=peak_dotcom, lw=1))
ax1.annotate('AI Era High\n(Q4 2024)', xy=(ai_peak_offset, max(ndx_ai_y)), 
            xytext=(ai_peak_offset+1.5, max(ndx_ai_y)+15),
            fontsize=9, color=peak_ai, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=peak_ai, lw=1))

ax1.set_ylabel('NASDAQ Index\n(base = 100)', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color=grey)
ax1.set_title('Dot-com vs. AI Bubble: A Comparative Anatomy', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', color='#222222', pad=12)
ax1.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, facecolor='white', edgecolor=light_grey, fontsize=10)
ax1.grid(True, linestyle='-', alpha=0.3, color=grid_color)
ax1.set_ylim(0, 360)
ax1.set_xlim(-1, 25)
ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax1.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax1.spines['left'].set_color(light_grey)
ax1.spines['bottom'].set_color(light_grey)

# ---- Panel 2: P/E Ratio ----
ax2 = axes[1]
ax2.set_facecolor(bg_color)
ax2.plot(pe_dotcom_x, pe_dotcom_y, color=dotcom_color, linewidth=2.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Dot-com')
ax2.plot(pe_ai_x, pe_ai_y, color=ai_color, linewidth=2.5, marker='s', markersize=5, label='AI Era')

# Peak markers
ax2.axvline(x=dotcom_peak_offset, color=peak_dotcom, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.7)
ax2.axvline(x=ai_peak_offset, color=peak_ai, linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, alpha=0.7)

# Annotation for P/E magnitude difference
ax2.annotate('Dot-com P/E peaked at 105×', xy=(12, 105.2), xytext=(14, 115),
            fontsize=9, color=peak_dotcom, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=peak_dotcom, lw=1))
ax2.annotate('AI-era P/E peaked at 40×', xy=(15, 40.3), xytext=(17, 50),
            fontsize=9, color=peak_ai, fontweight='bold',
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='->', color=peak_ai, lw=1))

ax2.set_ylabel('P/E Ratio\n(trailing 12m)', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold', color=grey)
ax2.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True, facecolor='white', edgecolor=light_grey, fontsize=10)
ax2.grid(True, linestyle='-', alpha=0.3, color=grid_color)
ax2.set_ylim(0, 130)
ax2.set_xlim(-1, 25)
ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax2.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax2.spines['left'].set_color(light_grey)
ax2.spines['bottom'].set_color(light_grey)

# ---- Panel 3: IPO Counts ----
ax3 = axes[2]
ax3.set_facecolor(bg_color)

bar_width = 1.2
ax3.bar([x - bar_width/2 for x in ipo_dotcom_x], ipo_dotcom_y, width=bar_width, 
        color=dotcom_color, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, label='Dot-com')
ax3.bar([x + bar_width/2 for x in ipo_ai_x], ipo_ai_y, width=bar_width, 
        color=ai_color, alpha=0.85, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.5, label='AI Era')
